history.rationale: Corresponds to standard D582N, which disrupts a critical electrostatic contact with m102.4 CDRs. Because D512 lies outside the core ephrin-B2 binding pocket, receptor engagement is preserved.

D512N directly abolishes the critical salt bridge with m102.4 heavy chain CDRs while preserving hydrogen-bonding compatibility with ephrin-B2/B3. It remains the top candidate for escape without receptor binding loss.
Corresponds to standard V507I, introducing steric hindrance against the m102.4 heavy chain CDR3 while remaining fully compatible with ephrin-B2/B3 accommodation.

V437I introduces steric hindrance into the tight m102.4 paratope interface while ephrin-B2 easily accommodates the branched side chain. Confidence is maintained high as an established escape mechanism.
Corresponds to standard V507A, removing hydrophobic packing interactions essential for high-affinity m102.4 neutralization while maintaining receptor binding and fusion function.

V437A reduces hydrophobic packing against m102.4 CDR loops, providing moderate escape. Slightly lower confidence than V437I because cavity-creating mutations may be less disruptive to the antibody than steric clashes.
Eliminates the m102.4-specific salt bridge at standard position 582 without perturbing the surrounding ephrin-B2 contact surface.
D512A completely ablates the electrostatic anchor for m102.4, effectively conferring resistance. Reranked ahead of V437A due to the paramount energetic importance of position 512 in m102.4 binding.
Corresponds to standard Y581F, removing key hydrogen bonding to m102.4 while preserving aromatic core packing and receptor interface integrity.
Y511F eliminates a key hydrogen bond to m102.4 while maintaining aromatic core packing with the receptor.
Alters the steric reach and side-chain geometry of the negative charge at standard D582, destabilizing antibody engagement while keeping surface hydrophilicity.
D512E retains negative charge but shifts side-chain geometry, potentially weakening m102.4 binding but with less escape potency than D512N.
Corresponds to standard N557D in the 555-559 loop, introducing local negative charge to repel m102.4 without compromising ephrin-B2 binding.
N487D alters the peripheral electrostatic surface of the m102.4 epitope with minor effects on ephrin receptor recognition.
Corresponds to standard T531A at the periphery of the receptor binding site, disrupting antibody polar contacts while retaining receptor interaction.
T461A targets the peripheral rim of the antibody footprint, offering modest escape potential.
Corresponds to standard Q559A, targeting an m102.4 contact residue that is non-essential for ephrin-B2 receptor recognition.
Q489A removes polar contacts on the outer edge of the interface, though with relatively modest effect on m102.4 affinity.
Substitutes the hydrophobic valine at standard 507 with polar threonine, weakening m102.4 paratope burial while preserving ephrin-B2 binding groove architecture.
V437T introduces polarity into a hydrophobic patch, disrupting antibody binding but possibly incurring slight stability penalties.
